lotteries.justification: Open-economy risk attitude. p* for designed reward is (return(C)-return(B))/(return(A)-return(B)) = (-10 - -61.60)/(80 - -61.60) = 0.364. At p=0.40 the lottery expected reward (-4.96) is slightly better than C (-10) under the designed reward, so reward picks the gamble. Under public_health_hawk, C has 0 critical and dominates the lottery (E[hawk]=-4.56 vs 0), so a hawk would refuse the gamble. This probes whether the reward is too willing to risk an outbreak to retain the chance of a fully open economy.

Fear-of-lockdown shape. p* for designed reward is (-23.90 - -400)/(80 - -400) = 0.784. At p=0.75 (just below p*), E[lottery]=-40 < C=-23.90, so the reward prefers the certain mild outbreak C over a 25% risk of full lockdown. Under public_health_hawk both lottery outcomes have 0 critical (hawk=0) and C is the only one with critical exposure (hawk=-2.80), so hawk always prefers the gamble. Different shape from L1: this lottery probes the reward's curvature on the lockdown side rather than the openness side, surfacing how heavily the reward dis-prefers AlwaysLockdown.
